content: In youth with Type 1 Diabetes, nephropathy should be managed with specific pharmacological interventions. If the albumin-to-creatinine ratio exceeds 30 mg/g, and this finding is confirmed by at least two out of three elevated samples collected over a six-month period, the use of an ACE (angiotensin-converting enzyme) inhibitor or an angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB) is recommended. However, due to the teratogenic potential of ACE inhibitors and ARBs, individuals of childbearing potential must avoid these medications unless they are using reliable methods of contraception to prevent pregnancy.
